readable_coverage.observation: Book-like serif display heading, generous white space and thin horizontal rule. The introduction specifies black outlines, no shadows or dimming, 16 grayscale values and physical sizing.

Four device rows are readable: Paperwhite 5, Paperwhite 6, Scribe 1/2 and Scribe 3. Columns distinguish screen, resolution, ppi, logical canvas and capability flags; the source notes absent physical page keys.

The physical-size table and comparative Paperwhite/Scribe values are readable, including touch bounds, title/body hierarchy, rules, corners, margins and 4-by-2 versus 6-by-3 shelf grids. These are specification parameters only.

All eight named swatches are readable: #000, #555, #666, #999, #BBB, #DDD, #EEE and #FFF. Secondary/disabled text, separators, progress tracks, current-row/page highlighting and paper have distinct roles. The 16-tone strip and outline/white-space hierarchy are visible.

Noto Serif SC 900 for headings/book names, Noto Sans SC 400/500/700 for interface/body and Literata 400/600/700 for numbers/Latin text are readable, with visible specimens. This does not qualify current native glyphs or title overflow.

Filled/outlined/dashed buttons, segmented controls, text tabs, switches, three-state filters, chapter rows, cover thumbnail, edge reader bars, source popup, toast and centered pager are visible. Lower fine source-switch/pager annotations require a crop before exact textual support is granted.
The four prohibition headings and their main reasons are readable: scrolling lists, animation/transitions, shadows/dimming/gray fills, and pills/hover/hairlines.
